Linear combinations of group effects

Source: R/contrast.R
trop_contrast.Rd

trop_contrast() calculates linear combinations of the estimates of trop_effects() or trop() objects. Examples are the mean effect of event times 0 to 3, or the difference between two cohorts. The function uses the bootstrap draws of the objects. It does not calculate the estimator again.

Usage

trop_contrast(x, contrasts, conf_level = NULL, ci = c("normal", "percentile"))

Arguments

x

A trop_effects object, a trop object, or a named list of such objects, all with a bootstrap.

contrasts

A named numeric vector of coefficients, with the names of the estimates. A named list of such vectors gives one combination for each element. An estimate that is not in a vector has the coefficient 0.

conf_level

The confidence level. The default is the level of the first object.

ci

Use "normal" or "percentile". Refer to trop().

Value

A data frame of class trop_effects with one row for each combination and the columns contrast, estimate, std.error, conf.low, conf.high, band.low, band.high, and n_draws. The attribute coefficients is the matrix of coefficients.

Details

For each combination, the estimate is the sum of the coefficients times the estimates. Each draw gets the same sum of its draws. A draw without a value for an estimate with a coefficient that is not 0 has no value for the combination. The standard error is the standard deviation of the draws.

All objects must have the same bootstrap draws. Draw b of each object must use the same units. Refer to the section Joint draws of trop_stepdown(). The names of the estimates are the names of trop_stepdown(). For one trop_effects object, the names are the groups, for example "0" and "1" for event times. For a named list, the names have the form "event: 0".

The result is a trop_effects object. Thus, trop_stepdown() can adjust the p-values of the combinations, and vcov() gives their covariance.

See also

trop_effects(), trop_stepdown()

Examples

sim <- trop_simulate(n_units = 20, n_periods = 12, n_treated = 5,
                     n_post = 3, effect = 1, seed = 1)
fit <- trop(sim, "y", "d", "unit", "time",
            lambda = c(time = 0.2, unit = 0.5, nn = 0.5),
            n_boot = 50, seed = 1, control = trop_control(threads = 1))
ev <- trop_effects(fit, by = "event_time")
trop_contrast(ev, list(mean_0_2 = c("0" = 1, "1" = 1, "2" = 1) / 3,
                       last_minus_first = c("2" = 1, "0" = -1)))
#> TROP effects by contrast
#>   Each row is a linear combination of estimates.
#>          contrast estimate std.error conf.low conf.high band.low band.high
#>          mean_0_2    1.119    0.2020   0.7228    1.5147   0.7323    1.5052
#>  last_minus_first   -1.455    0.5742  -2.5801   -0.3294  -2.5531   -0.3564
#>  n_draws
#>       50
#>       50
#> Bootstrap: 50 draws. The band is simultaneous (sup-t) at the 95% level. It uses the 50 draws with a value for all rows.
